contradictions.subject: EX34-23 versus accepted PR #65 correction

documentation_laundering.note: Current translation docs explicitly distinguish Stage 3C primitives from Stage 5A persisted publication/read activation. Later descriptions do not make PR #31/#32/#34 mechanisms appear older than their introduction. R6 retrospective claims are not pre-credited.

F1.title: Persistent translation/storage identity with live downstream use
F1.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the boundary is unused, duplicates another authority, or materially blocks current development without an accepted consumer.
F1.contrary_found: The accepted R1 contracts already require source freshness/origin separation, and current Stage 5/raw/bundle paths still consume the same persistent identities or semantics. Later use is corroboration, not retroactive authority.
F1.effect: Intentional foundation; neither complexity nor deferred external rollout makes the boundary a defect.

F2.title: Bundle/compiler semantic boundary with current runtime consumer
F2.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the primitive remained dead scaffolding, encoded a closed-locale assumption, or required replacement before any real consumer could use it.
F2.contrary_found: Current Stage 5 publication and persisted-first runtime reads reuse the compiler/version/store boundaries. The exact later v2 identity extends rather than invalidates the Stage 3 primitive.
F2.effect: Intentional foundation with demonstrated retrofit value.

F3.title: Failure/integrity boundary retained by current runtime
F3.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the boundary masks programming/configuration errors or converts an optional dependency into a mandatory outage.
F3.contrary_found: Current code keeps unexpected failures visible and degrades only classified storage conditions; the known overbroad code-less branch is separately classified as EX32-17.

A1.title: Historical rollout/process alternative
A1.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the step was unauthorized mandatory external work unrelated to the then-selected runtime rollout, or that it remains a feature-development gate after the later user reprioritization.
A1.contrary_found: Accepted R2 already establishes the then production-first cadence as a coherent alternative with direct-user authority unproven. Current MIGRATIONS keeps schema-first ordering only for actual external schema-dependent rollout.
A1.effect: Acceptable historical alternative; no direct-user approval is inferred and PR #50 is not applied retroactively.

A2.title: Implementation/optimization alternative
A2.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the mechanism creates correctness loss, hides errors, or imposes material complexity with no current or plausible accepted consumer.
A2.contrary_found: Current tests/code retain the mechanism without a demonstrated correctness regression; where a specific defect exists it is classified on its own record.

A3.title: Deliberate staged deferral
A3.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the omitted consumer was required for correctness of the then-current Stage 3 slice or that the omission caused a current defect.
A3.contrary_found: The later Stage 5A chain explicitly owns persisted bundle publication/runtime reads and now consumes these primitives. Stage 3C was documented as primitives, not end-to-end generation/runtime switching.
A3.effect: Acceptable staged boundary, not a missing-current-stage defect.

D_EN.title: Whitespace-wrapped canonical-English persistence bypass
D_EN.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that database constraints and verifier trim locale identity before the English comparison, or that another current schema constraint makes whitespace-wrapped values impossible.
D_EN.contrary_found: Current immutable migration and db/schema.ts still use `btrim(locale) <> '' AND lower(locale) <> 'en'`; `' en '` passes. The current production verifier likewise queries `lower(locale) = 'en'` without trimming. No later migration 0011+ exists.
D_EN.effect: Real current defect in the record's English-exclusion/verification implementation.

D_CODELESS.title: Overbroad code-less PostgreSQL availability classification
D_CODELESS.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that every code-less pg connect Error denotes availability loss and cannot represent configuration/programming failures.
D_CODELESS.contrary_found: PR #39 explicitly narrowed this behavior; current tests require generic driver/configuration Error to remain visible and accept only known transport/termination shapes.
D_CODELESS.effect: Real historical original defect, corrected later by accepted EX39-08/09/10.

D_NS.title: Prototype-sensitive bundle namespace validation
D_NS.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that PR #65 or another later change replaced bundle compiler namespace lookup with own-property membership.
D_NS.contrary_found: PR #65 changed `sources.ts` only. Current `app/localization/bundles.ts` still checks `canonicalEnglishCatalog[namespace]` in `assertBundleScope`/`descriptorMap`, so inherited names can pass the unknown-namespace guard exactly as PR #34 review described.
D_NS.effect: Real current defect in the bundle compiler path. The accepted PR #65 fix is analogous forward evidence, not a fix for this record.

J_STORE.title: Persisted bundle trust-boundary integrity correction
J_STORE.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the database adapter could only ever receive compiler-produced, immutable, already-verified rows, making independent read/write verification redundant.
J_STORE.contrary_found: The initial PR #34 store accepted stored/supplied version/content directly. Commit c24c2433 added recomputation and version matching at the persistence boundary, which later Stage 5 persisted reads/publication rely on.
J_STORE.effect: Justified fix of a concrete in-PR integrity defect.

S_EXT.title: Repository-recorded external operational evidence

S_EXT.effect: Reviewed supporting/provenance-only; not normative authority and not an unresolved architecture choice.
